question: Q16 — can the mean_reversion family be calibrated AT ALL? (docs/QUESTIONS.md)
notes: The first mean_reversion batch could not be calibrated: 24 of 30 nulls traded less than the 121-trade min-n, so the null cohort was mostly could-not-look and the empirical bar (+0.50R) was built from noise. That is a fact about the FAMILY, not the batch - these grids trade too rarely to grade. This run loosens the triggers (higher oversold, weaker regime filter, longer holds) on the broad universe purely to raise trade COUNT, and runs 300 nulls. If the nulls still cannot clear min-n, the honest conclusion is that mean_reversion cannot be graded per-trade on this history and needs a different yardstick - which is a real finding and blocks promoting it either way.
